citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit
cited_name: Tanner v. Commissioner of Social Security
explanation: Mangum cites Tanner only as a 'see also' noting it presumed without deciding that the mandate rule reaches agencies; supporting, non-controlling authority. Tanner itself states it is unpublished and not binding.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
explanation: Beuns says the facts 'fit squarely within our precedent, which holds' the $500-per-device rule, citing only unpublished Gilmore, and affirms on it; a different defendant and case. Unpublished Sixth Circuit opinions are not binding.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Six Circuit
explanation: Slusser mentions Page only as a case the petitioner cited and expressly distinguishes it (plea voluntariness challenge); it is not followed, let alone treated as controlling.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
explanation: Lumaj cites Hasanaj in a footnote only to show counsel had notice the argument was rejected; the court names published Denko as the controlling precedent, not Hasanaj.

citing_name: Barbourville Nursing Home v. United States Department of Health & Huma
citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
cited_name: Livingston Care Center v. Dept. of Health & Human Services
explanation: Barbourville cites Livingston as 388 F.3d 168, the published version of that opinion (own knowledge: the F. App'x decision was later published), and merely quotes it describing the regulation's preventive focus, in the text given.

citing_name: U.S. Oil Recovery Site Potentially Responsible Parties Grp. v. R.R. Co
citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit
explanation: Ochoa-Perez, an Anders dismissal, is never cited; the citation at 614 F. App'x 789 is to Bach v. Texas State University, a different decision sharing the page. Though the court calls its unpublished decisions 'our precedent', the named decision was not relied on.

citing_name: Brand Servs., L.L.C. v. Irex Corp.
citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit
explanation: Brand Services cites Curry with a parenthetical as an example of discretion to deny untimely motions to compel, then rules the other way on published authority; illustrative, not controlling.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit
cited_name: Northwest Title Agency, Inc. v. Minnesota Department of Commerce
explanation: King cites the unpublished per curiam Northwest Title (F. App'x) only with a 'See' signal, as a parenthetical quoting the published Athens/Alpha rule; Athens/Alpha is the authority relied on. Illustrative use, not treated as binding; different litigation.
